name: Lampasas
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Lampasas, TX 2026
seo_desc: Christmas events for kids in Lampasas, TX for 2026: the HoliDazzle parade, Christmas on the Creek, library story times and more, checked on host sites.
lede: Lampasas keeps Christmas small-town and close to the creek: a lighted parade around the Courtyard Square, then a night of lights, Santa and hot cocoa along Sulphur Creek.
celebrates: Lampasas celebrates Christmas on two Saturdays. The first Saturday of December brings Carol of Lights and the HoliDazzle Lighted Christmas Parade to the Historic Courtyard Square, with floats, marching bands, vintage cars, horses, and Santa and Mrs. Claus riding at the end. The following Saturday, Christmas on the Creek fills W.M. Brook Park with Santa's Village, giant 12 Days of Christmas cards, a lighted Nativity, Candy Cane Lane, hot cocoa and a snow machine. The lights and park displays along Sulphur Creek stay up from Thanksgiving until New Year's, so families can also visit on a quiet weeknight.
lastyear: Last December the first Saturday of the month followed the same pattern. The Lampasas Dispatch Record's preview of Carol of Lights listed a farmers market, car show, museum displays, children's activities, food, Santa and Mrs. Claus, the Snow Queen pageant and student carolers, with the courthouse lighting at 6 pm and the parade at 6:30 pm. Christmas on the Creek kept its lights on after city leaders found the money to keep the tree lighting going for the 2025 season, according to KXXV.
facts: Christmas on the Creek is about 11 years old. According to its chairperson in a 2025 KXXV interview, a group of citizens started it because they wanted to see Sulphur Creek used during the Christmas holidays. The city of Lampasas took over the tree lights in 2016 because they had to meet electrical codes and needed professional electricians. W.M. Brook Park is a 12 acre greenbelt with an amphitheater, playground, picnic area and a hike-and-bike trail.
trains: We did not find a Christmas train ride in Lampasas for 2026, and the town's holiday events are parades, lights and library and museum programs. If your kids are chasing a train, Rally's Killeen and Temple pages cover the nearest options in Bell County, including Santa at the Depot at the Temple Railroad and Heritage Museum. Check those pages for dates, times and prices before you drive.
traditions: Floats, marching bands, vintage cars and horses roll around the Courtyard Square at 6:30 pm on the first Saturday of December.
The Chamber and Lampasas County Museum celebrate the first Saturday of December on the Historic Courtyard Square.
Santa's Village, a lighted Nativity and Candy Cane Lane fill W.M. Brook Park along Sulphur Creek.
The lights and park displays stay up from Thanksgiving until New Year's.
The Lampasas County Museum holds an annual tour of decorated homes with a tree and gingerbread house contest.
kidfact: Santa's Village at Christmas on the Creek sits right beside Sulphur Creek, and the lights stretch all the way between Highway 190 and Highway 281.
faq: When is the Lampasas Christmas parade in 2026?
The HoliDazzle Lighted Christmas Parade is on Saturday, December 5, 2026, at 6:30 pm around the Historic Courtyard Square. Carol of Lights activities start at 9 am the same day.
Where can kids see Christmas lights in Lampasas?

Along Sulphur Creek at W.M. Brook Park, between Highway 190 (Key Avenue) and Highway 281. Vision Lampasas says the lights and park displays are open from Thanksgiving until New Year's, with the big Christmas on the Creek night on December 12.
Can kids meet Santa in Lampasas?
Santa and Mrs. Claus ride in the HoliDazzle parade on December 5, and Santa's Village is part of Christmas on the Creek on December 12.
Are there Christmas events at the Lampasas library?
Yes. The Lampasas Public Library lists a Winter Holidays Pre-K Story Time on December 3 and a Christmas Family Story Time on December 5, both at 10:15 am.
Is there more to do near Lampasas?
Many Lampasas families also drive to Killeen, Copperas Cove and Temple for trains, parades and lights. Those towns have their own Rally pages.
